3

The Python notebook (notebook.html) runs Python 3 in the browser — without installation, server or internet connection. It works like Jupyter: notebooks with code and text cells, results directly below the code, plots, tables. A console runs single commands.

Included libraries: numpy, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, scipy, scikit-learn, sympy, networkx, lxml, beautifulsoup4, pyyaml, openpyxl, xlrd, regex, requests, sqlite3, SQLAlchemy, pykeepass, nzpy, micropip; for office files python-docx, python-pptx, XlsxWriter (also as pandas' Excel writer), pypdf and icalendar; for databases over the relay pg8000 (PostgreSQL) and PyMySQL (MySQL/MariaDB), also through SQLAlchemy; Jinja2 (with MarkupSafe), Markdown, tabulate and tqdm. They are loaded when they are imported for the first time; numpy, pandas and matplotlib are prepared in the background after the start. The first start takes a few seconds; the status at the top right shows when Python is ready.

Notebooks

  • Open (Ctrl+O) opens a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) or a Python script. In scripts, # %% starts a code cell and # %% [markdown] a text cell (the format of VS Code, Spyder and Jupytext); a script without markers becomes one cell. Raw cells (for nbconvert) are shown as plain text, marked Raw, and saved unchanged.
  • Save (Ctrl+S) saves the notebook as .ipynb (with outputs): directly into the file in Chrome/Edge on the desktop, as a download in Firefox and on Android. Save as saves under a new name. Export… downloads the notebook as a Python script (.py), as an HTML page with code, Markdown and outputs (tables, charts) that opens in any browser, as an HTML page without code (a report of the results), or prints it (PDF: choose "Save as PDF" as the printer).
  • New starts an empty notebook.

Cells

  • + Code and + Markdown insert a cell below the selected one; the buttons next to a cell run it (▶), switch its type (M / { }), move it (↑ ↓) or delete it (✕).
  • Markdown cells show formatted text after running; double-click to edit them again.
  • ▶▶ Run all runs all cells from the top; Clear outputs removes all results.
Key In a cell (editing)
Shift+Enter run and go to the next cell (a new one at the end)
Ctrl+Enter run and stay
Alt+Enter run and insert a new cell below
Escape leave the editor (command mode)
Tab / Shift+Tab indent / unindent (4 spaces)
Ctrl+Alt+I insert a tab character

In command mode (a cell is selected, the cursor is not in it) the keys work as in JupyterLab: Enter edits, A/B insert a cell above/below, M/Y/R make the cells Markdown, code or raw cells, ↑/↓ (or K/J) select the previous/next cell.

Several cells: Shift+↑/Shift+↓ (or Shift+K/Shift+J) and Shift+click select several cells, Ctrl+A all of them. The keys then apply to all selected cells: Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter and Alt+Enter run them, C copies, X cuts, V pastes below (Shift+V above), D, D (twice) or Delete deletes, Shift+M merges them into one cell (one selected cell: with the next one), Ctrl+Shift+↑/↓ moves them.

Running: cells run one after another; waiting cells show [*]. Stop on error (on by default, next to ▶▶ Run all): when a cell raises an error, the cells waiting after it are not run, as in Jupyter. Switched off, they run anyway.

Outputs: printed text, errors (only your code in the traceback), the result of the last line, tables (pandas), plots (matplotlib, also without plt.show()), HTML and Markdown. HTML and Markdown from notebooks are shown without scripts.

In command mode, Z or Ctrl+Z (and ↶ in the toolbar) undoes the last cell operation: inserting, deleting, moving, changing the type, clearing outputs; Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y or ↷ redoes it. Inside a cell, Ctrl+Z undoes typing in that cell. Running cells is not undone.

In Slideshow mode every cell shows a slide type (slide, sub-slide, fragment, skip, notes – stored in the notebook like in Jupyter), and 🎞️ Slides opens the notebook as a reveal.js presentation in the app.

Spelling: with a language chosen in the ABC selector of the header, Markdown cells are checked completely and code cells in their comments and strings; right-click an underlined word for suggestions ().

Console

The Console tab runs single commands in the same Python session as the notebook (variables are shared). Enter runs, Shift+Enter starts a new line, ↑/↓ recall earlier commands. Clear empties the console.

Terminal

The Terminal tab has a bash-like shell on Python's file system (the same files as the Files panel and the cells; it lives only in memory). It is written in Python and runs in the notebook's Python, so it works offline everywhere.

  • Commands: ls, cd, pwd, cat, cp, mv, rm, mkdir, rmdir, touch, find (-name, -iname, -type, -maxdepth), du, head, tail, wc, grep (Python regular expressions; -i -v -n -c -l -r -o -w -x -F), sed (s/// with g, i and a number, d, p, =, q; addresses N, $, /re/ and ranges; -n, -i, -e), sort (-r -n -u -k -t -f), uniq (-c -d -u), cut (-d -f -c), tr (ranges, classes, -d -s), diff (-u, -q), echo, printf, tar (-c -x -t, -z -j -J, -f, -C), zip (-r), unzip (-l -d), python script.py / python -c …, pip install (micropip; needs the network), mount / umount (archives of the archive manager, see Archives in Python), env, export, unset, history, clear, which, basename, dirname, date, sleep, true, false and help.
  • Command lines are split like in a POSIX shell (shlex): quotes, \, comments (#), pipes |, redirections >, >>, <, 2>, 2>&1, &&, || and ;, globs (*, ?, […]), variables (NAME=value, $NAME, ${NAME}, $?, ~) and !N (a line of the history). There are no control structures (if, for, while), no background jobs and no other programs.
  • Scripts: sh script.sh arguments (also bash, source or ./script.sh) runs the lines of a script in this shell with $1…$9, $# and $@; set -e stops at the first error, exit ends the script. Scripts from an archive run after mounting it, e.g. mount data.zip && sh /mnt/data.zip/run.sh.
  • Keys: ↑/↓ history, Tab completes commands and paths (twice: shows the choices), Ctrl+C cancels the line (or interrupts a running command where possible), Ctrl+L clears the screen, Ctrl+U deletes the line, Ctrl+A/Ctrl+E start/end of the line.
  • less shows a file or the output of a pipe (… | less): Space/PgDn and b/PgUp page, ↑/↓/j/k line, g/G start/end, /text searches, n/N next/previous match, q quits.
  • nano edits a file: type, cursor keys, Ctrl+O saves (asks for the name), Ctrl+X exits (asks about unsaved changes), Ctrl+W searches, Ctrl+K cuts the line, Ctrl+U pastes. Changes are written to Python's file system.
  • In cells: await suite.shell.run("ls -l | head") runs a command line and prints its output (less shows the text, nano works only in the Terminal tab).

Files and packages

The Files panel shows Python's working folder (/home/pyodide):

  • Upload… copies files from your computer into the folder (or drop them onto the window), so Python can read them, e.g. with pd.read_csv('data.csv').
  • Click a file to download it (e.g. results written by Python), × deletes it, folders open with a click.
  • Install wheel… installs further Python packages from wheel files (.whl): pure-Python packages from PyPI, or packages built for Pyodide. They stay installed until the page is closed (also after a restart).

The files only exist while the page is open: download results you want to keep.

Other applications of the suite open files from this file system and save files into it (Open / Save as, section Python notebooks (in memory), see ): the notebook then shows what is asked for – the folder and the name for saving, or the files to open – with the reminder that the files exist only in memory. Save in the other application writes the file here again. A restart of Python asks first while such files are open elsewhere.

↗ next to a file in the files panel (Open with…) opens it in another application of the suite (e.g. the text editor or spreadsheet); saving there writes it back into the Python file system.

Adding packages at runtime

Packages built for Pyodide that are not bundled – for example statsmodels, shapely, pyproj and scikit-image – can be added while the notebook runs. They must match the bundled Pyodide version (314.0.7); the files are in the Pyodide distribution at https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v314.0.7/full/<file>:

Package Files (in this order, after the bundled dependencies)
statsmodels patsy-1.0.2-py2.py3-none-any.whl, statsmodels-0.14.6-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl
shapely shapely-2.1.2-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl
pyproj pyproj-3.7.2-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl
scikit-image imageio-2.37.3-py3-none-any.whl, pywavelets-1.9.0-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl, lazy_loader-0.5-py3-none-any.whl, scikit_image-0.26.0-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl
  • Offline: download the files once, then choose all of them at once with Install wheel… in the Files panel. They stay installed until the page is closed, also after a restart.
  • With internet access: install them in a cell (they are gone after a restart):

python import micropip base = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v314.0.7/full/" await micropip.install([base + "patsy-1.0.2-py2.py3-none-any.whl", base + "statsmodels-0.14.6-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl"]) import statsmodels.api as sm

Pure-Python packages from PyPI (wheels ending in py3-none-any.whl) are added the same way; packages with compiled code need wheels built for Pyodide.

Archives in Python

Archives open in the can be mounted: their files appear as ordinary files below /mnt/<archive name>, so os, open, pathlib, shutil, glob and libraries such as pandas use them without anything special.

  • 📦 Mount archive… in the Files panel lists the open archives (or starts the archive manager to open or create one); the archive manager asks you to allow it. Mounted archives are listed in the Files panel; ⏏ unmounts one.
  • After every cell (and console command) new, changed and deleted files are written back into the archive. The archive manager marks it as changed – save the archive there to keep the changes.
  • The whole archive is copied into the notebook's memory (it asks first above 512 MiB). Changes made in the archive manager while the archive is mounted are not seen by the notebook: unmount and mount it again.
  • If the archive is closed or replaced in the archive manager, the notebook says so after the next cell; the files stay in /mnt, but further changes are no longer saved into the archive. A restart of Python unmounts all archives.

In code, the module suite does the same (awaited in a cell):

py

suite.archives.mount() can only reach archive managers that are already open (in the overview: its tabs; otherwise the archive manager windows started from the notebook, or the one that started it): to open or create an archive, use the button. Notebooks that should also run in a regular Jupyter installation import suite in a try block and use a folder there (see the example notebooks).

Network from Python

Python in the browser cannot open network connections itself; the notebook uses the for them. Set it in the Files panel under Network: Relay (address and token, or a connections file). The header shows what is possible:

  • Opened as a file (file://): requests goes through the relay – every request of the module, to any server, with all headers and cookies. Without a relay, requests only reaches servers that allow access from web pages (CORS). Sockets and SSH are not possible, and stopping a cell restarts Python.
  • 🔓 Network and interrupt – the notebook served by the relay (relay.py --serve): additionally sockets – the standard library's network modules work unchanged through the relay: smtplib (also starttls() and SMTP_SSL), imaplib, poplib, ftplib (passive mode), http.client, urllib.request and pure-Python database drivers. TLS is done by the relay, which checks the server's certificate (unless the code switches checking off). Listening sockets, UDP and raw sockets are not possible. Running cells can be interrupted.
py

SSH and SFTP (served by the relay only) use the suite's SSH engine with a subset of Fabric's Connection – so a notebook can use Fabric itself in a regular Jupyter installation:

py

connect_kwargs takes password, key_filename (a key file in the Files panel, OpenSSH or PEM format), passphrase or pkey_text (the key as text). The first connection to a server shows its host key fingerprint and asks whether to trust it (remembered in this browser); a changed key is asked for with a warning. The encryption is end to end between the browser and the server. suite.net.status() reports what is available.

Variables

Variables next to Files in the side panel lists the variables of the running Python session after every run: name, type (with the dtype of NumPy arrays), size (rows × columns of DataFrames and arrays, the length of lists and strings) and a short value (the column names of DataFrames). Modules, functions, classes and names starting with _ are left out. A click on a DataFrame, Series or array (▦) shows it as a table (up to 500 rows and 50 columns).

Interactive widgets

Cells can show controls with the usual ipywidgets API (built in, nothing to install):

py

Available are sliders (IntSlider, FloatSlider, FloatLogSlider, range sliders, SelectionSlider), number and text fields, Checkbox, ToggleButton, Dropdown, RadioButtons, Select, SelectMultiple, ToggleButtons, Button (on_click), ColorPicker, DatePicker, Play, progress bars, Label, HTML, Output (with out: collects prints, displays and figures), the containers HBox, VBox, GridBox, Tab and Accordion, as well as interact, interactive, interact_manual, fixed, observe, link and dlink. from IPython.display import display, clear_output, HTML, Markdown works too.

Prints and errors of callbacks outside an Output widget appear below the cell that created the widget. Saved notebooks keep the state of the widgets (in the format of Jupyter): after opening, the controls are shown as they were but are inactive until the cell runs again; the same applies after a restart. Custom widget libraries (e.g. ipyleaflet, bqplot) are not supported.

Stop and restart

While cells run, the toolbar shows a stop button (also I, I in command mode):

  • ⏹ Interrupt – when the notebook is served by the relay (relay.py --serve, see ): the running cell stops with a KeyboardInterrupt, as in Jupyter; variables and imports are kept. The cells waiting after it are not run. Code inside a long single call of compiled code (one huge numpy operation) stops when that call returns.
  • ⏹ Stop – when the notebook is opened as a file (file://): browsers only let a page interrupt Python when it is served with special headers, so stopping means restarting Python after a confirmation; variables are lost.

⟲ Restart (also 0, 0 in command mode) starts Python again at any time, also while code runs: all variables are lost, files and installed wheels stay.

Limits

  • Network: through the relay only (see Network from Python); sockets and SSH only when the notebook is served by the relay.
  • Only packages included in the suite or available as wheels can be used; packages with compiled code need wheels built for Pyodide.
